t2i_prompt: Isometric technical line drawing of <CONTENT>, a single piece of industrial process equipment, isolated and centred on a pure white square background with generous margin. Pure black lines of one uniform medium stroke weight, no fills, no shading, no hatching, no gradients, no text or labels. Elevated three-quarter isometric view so the top surfaces and their fittings read clearly; accurate ellipses, bolted flanges, small valves with handwheels, a pressure gauge, short pipe stubs entering from the frame edge. Engineering catalogue precision, clean vector look, high detail on fittings and plain smooth body surfaces, no ground plane, no people, mask-ready line art.
signature_idea: A single piece of plant equipment drawn as a precise black isometric line portrait, so it can be cut to a mask and tinted any brand colour.
strengths: reads as real process equipment to engineers: plausible nozzles, valves, manway, drive
uniform stroke and white ground make it trivially convertible to a token-coloured mask
calm, honest, no hype; fits a spec-reading audience
shows the customer's process (where PW is used) rather than Aquemi's kit, which suits an industry page
weaknesses: stroke is heavier than the brand's 1.5 px hairline when shown at small sizes
generic stainless-looking vessel; nothing says polypropylene or Aquemi
the PW point-of-use valve is not singled out, so the story (PW feeds the process) is not legible
no annotation, so it is decoration unless the page adds labels
brand_fit_why: Precise, calm, square-cornered line art that tints cleanly to navy or steel-blue, but stroke is a touch heavy and it lacks any accent or annotation tying it to the PW story.
